propositions.name: relative_motion_only
propositions.quote: The observed phenomena in this case depend only on the relative motion of the conductor and the magnet, while according to the usual conception, a distinction must be made
propositions.statement: The observed phenomena in the magnet and conductor case depend only on the relative motion of the two bodies, not on which one is in motion.

propositions.name: no_absolute_rest
propositions.quote: no properties of observed facts correspond to a concept of absolute rest ; but that for all coordinate systems for which the mechanical equations hold, the equivalent electrodynamical and optical equations hold also
propositions.statement: No properties of observed facts correspond to a concept of absolute rest, in mechanics or in electrodynamics.

propositions.name: light_velocity_independent_of_source
propositions.quote: light is propagated in vacant space, with a velocity c which is independent of the nature of motion of the emitting body
propositions.statement: Light is propagated in vacant space with a velocity c which is independent of the motion of the emitting body.

propositions.name: no_absolute_space_no_point_velocity
propositions.quote: we shall introduce neither a space absolutely at rest, and endowed with special properties, nor shall we associate a velocity-vector with a point in which electro-magnetic processes take place
propositions.statement: No space absolutely at rest with special properties is introduced, and no velocity-vector is associated with a point where electro-magnetic processes take place.

propositions.name: theory_rests_on_rigid_body_kinematics
propositions.quote: Like every other theory in electrodynamics, the theory is based on the kinematics of rigid bodies; in the enunciation of every theory, we have to do with relations between rigid bodies (co-ordinate system), clocks, and electromagnetic processes
propositions.statement: The theory is based on the kinematics of rigid bodies and on relations between rigid bodies, clocks, and electromagnetic processes.

propositions.name: stationary_system_is_newtonian
propositions.quote: Let us have a co-ordinate system, in which the Newtonian equations hold. For distinguishing this system from another which will be introduced hereafter, we shall always call it "the stationary system."
propositions.statement: The stationary co-ordinate system is defined as one in which the Newtonian equations hold.

propositions.name: rest_position_by_measuring_rod
propositions.quote: If a material point be at rest in this system, then its position in this system can be found out by a measuring rod, and can be expressed by the methods of Euclidean Geometry, or in Cartesian co-ordinates
propositions.statement: The position of a material point at rest in the stationary system can be found by a measuring rod and expressed by Euclidean Geometry or Cartesian co-ordinates.

propositions.name: time_conceptions_are_synchronism
propositions.quote: those of our conceptions, in which time plays a part, are always conceptions of synchronism . For example, we say that a train arrives here at 7 o'clock
propositions.statement: Every conception in which time plays a part is a conception of synchronism.

propositions.name: clocks_of_same_nature
propositions.quote: If an observer be stationed at B with a clock, —we should add that the clock is of the same nature as the one at A,— he can estimate the time of events occurring about B
propositions.statement: The clock at B is taken to be of the same nature as the one at A.

propositions.name: common_time_by_light_symmetry_definition
propositions.quote: This last time (i.e., common time) can be defined, if we establish by definition that the time which light requires in travelling from A to B is equivalent to the time which light requires in travelling from B to A
propositions.statement: Common time between A and B is established by definition that the time light requires from A to B equals the time light requires from B to A.

propositions.name: synchronism_definition_consistent
propositions.quote: We assume that this definition of synchronism is possible without involving any inconsistency, for any number of points, therefore the following relations hold
propositions.statement: The definition of synchronism is assumed to be free of inconsistency for any number of points.

propositions.name: principle_of_relativity
propositions.quote: The laws according to which the nature of physical systems alter are independent of the manner in which these changes are referred to two co-ordinate systems which have a uniform translatory motion relative to each other
propositions.statement: The laws of physical systems are independent of the choice among two co-ordinate systems which have a uniform translatory motion relative to each other.

propositions.name: constancy_of_light_in_stationary
propositions.quote: Every ray of light moves in the "stationary co-ordinate system" with the same velocity c , the velocity being independent of the condition whether this ray of light is emitted by a body at rest or in motion
propositions.statement: Every ray of light moves in the stationary co-ordinate system with the same velocity c, independent of whether emitted by a body at rest or in motion.

propositions.name: length_of_moving_rod_by_sync_clocks
propositions.quote: by means of clocks placed in a system at rest (the clocks being synchronous as defined in § 1), the points of this system where the ends of the rod to be measured occur at a particular time t
propositions.statement: The length of a moving rod is found by clocks at rest, synchronous as in section 1, marking the points of the stationary system where the ends occur at a particular time t.

propositions.name: silent_geometric_replaceability_rejected
propositions.quote: we silently assume that the lengths defined by these two operations are equal, or in other words, that at an epoch of time t , a moving rigid body is geometrically replaceable by the same body
propositions.statement: Ordinary kinematics silently assumes that the two operational lengths are equal, i.e. that at an epoch of time t a moving rigid body is geometrically replaceable by the same body at rest.

propositions.name: synchronism_has_no_absolute_significance
propositions.quote: we can attach no absolute significance to the concept of synchronism ; but two events which are synchronous when viewed from one system, will not be synchronous when viewed from a system moving relatively to this system
propositions.statement: Two events synchronous when viewed from one system are not synchronous when viewed from a system moving relatively to it, so synchronism has no absolute significance.

propositions.name: rods_and_clocks_identical_across_systems
propositions.quote: Let a rigid measuring rod, and a number of clocks be given to each of the systems, and let the rods and clocks in each be exactly alike each other
propositions.statement: The rigid measuring rod and clocks given to each of the two systems are exactly alike each other.

propositions.name: homogeneity_forces_linearity
propositions.quote: on account of the property of homogeneity which we ascribe to time and space, the equations must be linear
propositions.statement: Because time and space are homogeneous, the transformation equations must be linear.

propositions.name: light_relative_to_moving_origin_c_minus_v
propositions.quote: the ray of light moves relative to the origin of k with a velocity c-v , measured in the stationary system
propositions.statement: The ray of light moves relative to the origin of the moving system k with velocity c minus v, measured in the stationary system.

propositions.name: spherical_wave_stays_spherical_at_c
propositions.quote: the wave is propagated in the moving system with the same velocity c , and as a spherical wave. Therefore we show that the two principles are mutually reconcilable
propositions.statement: A spherical wave in system K is propagated in the moving system with the same velocity c and as a spherical wave, showing the two principles are reconcilable.

propositions.name: c_plays_part_of_infinite_velocity
propositions.quote: For a velocity larger than the velocity of light, our propositions become meaningless ; in our theory c plays the part of infinite velocity
propositions.statement: For a velocity larger than the velocity of light the propositions become meaningless, and c plays the part of infinite velocity.

propositions.name: equator_clock_slower_than_pole
propositions.quote: a clock placed at the equator must be slower by a very small amount than a similarly constructed clock which is placed at the pole, all other conditions being identical
propositions.statement: A clock placed at the equator must be slower by a very small amount than a similarly constructed clock at the pole, all other conditions being identical.

propositions.name: velocity_composition_bounded_by_c
propositions.quote: by combining two velocities, each of which is smaller than c , we obtain a velocity which is always smaller than c
propositions.statement: Combining two velocities each smaller than c yields a velocity which is always smaller than c.

propositions.name: parallel_transformation_forms_group
propositions.quote: We see that such a parallel transformation forms a group
propositions.statement: The parallel transformation of coordinates forms a group.

propositions.name: maxwell_equations_hold_in_moving_system
propositions.quote: The principle of Relativity requires that the Maxwell-Hertzian equations for pure vacuum shall hold also for the system k, if they hold for the system K
propositions.statement: The Principle of Relativity requires the Maxwell-Hertzian equations for pure vacuum to hold also in system k if they hold in system K.

propositions.name: fields_not_independent_of_frame_motion
propositions.quote: the electric and magnetic forces possess no existence independent of the nature of motion of the co-ordinate system
propositions.statement: The electric and magnetic forces possess no existence independent of the nature of motion of the co-ordinate system.

propositions.name: seat_of_electromagnetic_energy_meaningless
propositions.quote: Also the question about the seat of electromagnetic energy is seen to be without any meaning
propositions.statement: The question about the seat of electromagnetic energy is seen to be without any meaning.

propositions.name: charge_invariant_across_systems
propositions.quote: if its charge does not change thereby, when regarded from a system moving along with it, then the charge remains constant even when it is regarded from the stationary system K
propositions.statement: If a charge does not change when regarded from a co-moving system, the charge remains constant when regarded from the stationary system K.

propositions.name: no_velocity_exceeding_light
propositions.quote: For v=c , W is infinitely great. As our former result shows, velocities exceeding that of light can have no possibility of existence
propositions.statement: For v equal to c the electron's kinetic energy is infinitely great, so velocities exceeding that of light can have no possibility of existence.

propositions.name: mass_result_extends_to_ponderable
propositions.quote: for in our sense, a ponderable material point may be made into an electron by the addition of an electrical charge which may be as small as possible
propositions.statement: A ponderable material point can be made into an electron by adding an arbitrarily small charge, so the mass result also holds for ponderable material mass.

propositions.name: energy_principle_bounds_radiation_pressure
propositions.quote: The difference of these two expressions is, according to the Energy principle, the amount of work exerted, by the pressure of light per unit of time
propositions.statement: The difference between energy falling on and leaving the mirror equals, by the Energy principle, the work done by the pressure of light per unit time.
